question: What are customers contacting us about most, and what is changing?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Fraud and unauthorized activity is the single biggest thing customers contact us about — 1,337 of 5,425 contacts, 24.6% — and almost nothing about that picture is changing.**

After fraud, the volume sits in service and process failures rather than products: customer service experience (1,031 contacts, 19.0%), terms, information or communication (811, 14.9%), and then account opening or closure and funds hold or account restriction, tied at 626 each (11.5%). The shape of the demand matters as much as the ranking: three quarters of contacts (74.2%) end unresolved, and the most common thing the customer wants is money back — 38.8% are asking for a refund or a reversal.

On what is changing, the honest answer is: very little. Across the five largest reasons in the real complaint corpus, only one has a statistically meaningful direction over the full window — fees and charges, which is falling (t −2.11), from 7.9% of complaints in the prior quarter to 6.7% in the most recent one. The other four, fraud included, are flat.

The emerging-theme test says the same. Of the 8 themes with enough recent volume to be tested at the current as-of week, exactly one flagged: "Unhelpful customer service or multiple transfers" — 5 complaints in the last four weeks against 1.31 expected, a z of 2.75 and 4.17 times its baseline rate, and it holds up at eight weeks too. It is still small (28 complaints in total, 0.6% of the complaint corpus), but it is the one genuine movement in the data, and it is about customers being passed around rather than about any product. The practical read: this is a stable, chronic complaint mix, so the win is in fixing resolution and hand-offs, not in chasing a new issue.

caveats: The index holds two different corpora. The bulk is real written complaints about one bank covering July 2024 to June 2026; the rest is a set of synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from September 2023 only. Unfiltered totals mix the two, so they are a complaint-weighted view of contact demand, not a call-centre volume report.

All trend and emerging findings here are scoped to the real complaint corpus, because the synthetic conversations cover a single month and have no baseline to grow from. Those conversations also lift the softer, informational reasons - terms, information or communication in particular ranks higher unfiltered than it does among the real complaints alone.

There is no prior period before the data window, so the period-over-period deltas returned by the reason ranking are not meaningful; the direction and t-statistic from the monthly series are the trustworthy trend signal.

Only one theme cleared the emergence test and the expected number of false positives at this threshold is not zero, so the emerging finding should be treated as a signal to watch rather than a confirmed shift.
followups: Within the fraud volume, how much is account takeover versus scams where the customer authorised the payment, and are the two handled differently?
The unresolved rate is 74.2% overall - which reasons and products account for most of the repeat contact, and what would it take to close them first time?
